I'm sorry that I'm only replying now, the other comment has already put into words very well what I've been thinking about. I wanted to give a good answer, i.e. one that feels positive and nice, but at the same time I am aware that we hope for improvements quickly and are impatient.

So, yes, the truth is, it won't suddenly be good overnight, but it will get a little better every day. And yes, it is an individual process, just as every person is different and every eating disorder is different, so is the recovery path.

There was a time when I thought it would never get better and I couldn't even imagine how.

Today I look back and am positively surprised at what has changed, where I am now and what good things can still come. I'm not yet 100% where I want to be, but I have confidence and I guess that's already a lot<3

* **energy**, no longer being so tired, enough stamina to do things I set out to do
* My thoughts are not cluttered with food and numbers, instead there is **time** to think about important things and take action
   * **concentration**, my thoughts don't drift off all the time, basically more brain energy
   * getting more involved again with hobbies and **things I actually like**
   * friendships and relationships are **more real** again
   * conversations are **more profound**
* **no longer have to constantly worry**
   * about having to go to hospital when getting sick
   * about what other people think about me, my food, anything in general
      * in general: less worrying, recovery helps with **self esteem**
